intent.raw_query: Lisbon city break, $2500 couple, food and history, 5 days, May 2027, from Boston

experiences.name: Alfama Fado & Dinner Experience
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Portugal's soulful Fado music tradition with an intimate dinner at a traditional Fado house in the historic Alfama district. Enjoy authentic petiscos (Portuguese tapas), local wine, and live Fado performances by local artists in a centuries-old setting.

experiences.name: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Time Out Market, a curated food hall showcasing the best of Lisbon's culinary scene. Sample bacalhau (salt cod), pastéis de nata (custard tarts), ginjinha (cherry liqueur), and dishes from award-winning local chefs — all under one roof along the vibrant Ribeira waterfront.

experiences.name: São Jorge Castle & Mouraria Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore the 11th-century Moorish castle of São Jorge with panoramic views over Lisbon, then descend into the Mouraria neighborhood — the city's oldest and most multicultural quarter. A guided walking tour reveals layers of Moorish, medieval, and modern Portuguese history through its winding alleyways and hidden squares.

experiences.name: Belém Historical District & Pastéis de Belém
experiences.description: Visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery and the iconic Tower of Belém, two masterpieces of Manueline architecture dating to the Age of Discoveries. Afterward, stop at the legendary Pastéis de Belém bakery, open since 1837, for the original and most famous custard tarts in Portugal.

experiences.name: Mercado de Campo de Ourique & Príncipe Real Gourmet Walk
experiences.description: Discover Lisbon's upscale local food scene with a self-guided gourmet walk starting at the charming Mercado de Campo de Ourique, a neighborhood market beloved by locals. Continue to Príncipe Real for artisan cheese shops, organic wine bars, and specialty delis — a perfect way to eat like a true Lisboeta away from tourist crowds.
experiences.location: Campo de Ourique & Príncipe Real, Lisbon

trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight TP lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Take the Aerobus (Line 1, ~€4) or Metro Red Line (~€1.50 with Viva Viagem card) from Lisbon Humberto Delgado Airport to the city center. Check in at Lisbon City Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely walk through Baixa-Chiado, Lisbon's historic downtown grid. Stroll Rua Augusta, pass through the triumphal arch to Praça do Comércio by the Tagus River — free and scenic. Get your bearings and soak in the city atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour experience at Mercado da Ribeira (Av. 24 de Julho). Even on a budget, you can sample small dishes from multiple vendors — try a bifana (pork sandwich ~€3), a pastel de bacalhau (codfish cake ~€1.50), and a glass of house wine (~€2). Great introduction to Lisbon's food scene without committing to a sit-down restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick galão (milky coffee) and tosta mista (ham & cheese toast) at the airport café for ~€3–4 before landing.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick lunch near the hotel — look for a local tasca (tavern) offering a prato do dia (daily special) with soup, main, bread, and water for ~€7–9.
meals.dinner: Time Out Market Lisbon — budget ~€10–15 for a self-curated meal of small plates and a drink. Arrive before 20:00 to avoid peak crowds.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a reloadable Viva Viagem card at the airport Metro station (~€0.50 + load credit). Load €10 to cover tram, Metro, and bus rides for the first couple of days. Keep your first evening light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day at a neighborhood pastelaria near the hotel for a classic Lisbon breakfast. Then head to the São Jorge Castle & Mouraria Walking Tour. Explore the 11th-century Moorish hilltop castle (entry ~€15, or check for discounts with Lisbon Card). Enjoy panoramic 360° views over the city's terracotta rooftops and the Tagus River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from the castle into the Mouraria neighborhood — Lisbon's oldest and most multicultural quarter, the birthplace of Fado music. Wander its narrow alleyways, browse the Intendente square, and visit the free Igreja de São Cristóvão. Pop into a local grocery or market stall for affordable snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Experience authentic Fado in Mouraria. Look for a tasca that offers free Fado performances with dinner (common in this neighborhood on weekend evenings). Alternatively, visit Largo do Intendente and enjoy the lively street atmosphere. Have dinner at a nearby tasca.

meals.breakfast: Local pastelaria near hotel — galão + pastel de nata (custard tart) + toast ~€3–4.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch in the castle gardens or at a nearby café — buy a fresh bread roll, local cheese, and fruit from a mini-mercado for ~€4–5.
meals.dinner: Tasca in Mouraria — look for a set menu (ementa turística) with soup, grilled fish or meat, dessert, and a drink for ~€10–13. Try bacalhau à brás (shredded salted cod with eggs and potatoes).

day_by_day.notes: The Lisbon Card (1-day ~€22, 2-day ~€37) includes free entry to São Jorge Castle and unlimited public transport — worth considering if you plan multiple museum visits. Saturday mornings can be busy at the castle; aim to arrive by 09:30.

day_by_day.morning: Take Tram 28E (the iconic yellow tram, ~€3 single or free with Viva Viagem zapping) from Martim Moniz through Alfama, Graça, and Estrela. Ride the full route to experience Lisbon's hillside neighborhoods. Hop off at Miradouro da Graça for stunning free views over the city and castle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down through the Alfama district — Lisbon's oldest neighborhood, a labyrinth of medieval streets. Visit the free exterior of the Sé de Lisboa (Lisbon Cathedral, founded 1147). Browse the Sunday Feira da Ladra flea market at Campo de Santa Clara (free entry, open until ~17:00) for vintage finds, local crafts, and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Bairro Alto for the evening. This bohemian hilltop neighborhood comes alive on Sunday evenings. Walk the streets and enjoy the free atmosphere. Have dinner at one of the many affordable tasca-style restaurants before heading back.

meals.breakfast: Sunday treat — sit-down breakfast at a café in Graça neighborhood near the miradouro. Coffee, fresh orange juice, and a croissant ~€5.
meals.lunch: Grab a bifana or prego (beef sandwich) from a street stall near Feira da Ladra for ~€3–4. Add a Super Bock beer for ~€1.50.
meals.dinner: Bairro Alto tasca — try caldo verde (green soup), grilled sardines or frango assado (roast chicken), and a carafe of house red wine. Budget ~€12–15 total.

day_by_day.notes: Tram 28E is very popular with tourists — beware of pickpockets and consider taking it early (before 10:00) to avoid overcrowding. The Feira da Ladra flea market only operates on Tuesdays and Saturdays/Sundays — Sunday is perfect timing.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train from Cais do Sodré station to Belém (15 min, ~€1.50 with Viva Viagem). Begin the Belém Historical District experience. Visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery (entry ~€10, or free on Sunday mornings before 14:00 — note this is Monday, so full price applies). Marvel at the extraordinary Manueline Gothic architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Belém — walk to the iconic Torre de Belém (Tower of Belém, entry ~€6) along the Tagus riverfront. Then visit the nearby Monument to the Discoveries (Padrão dos Descobrimentos, entry ~€6 or exterior only for free). Stroll the riverside promenade and enjoy the maritime atmosphere. Visit the famous Pastéis de Belém bakery (Rua de Belém 84) — the original since 1837 — for a pastel de nata fresh from the oven (~€1.30 each).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center by train. Spend the evening in the Cais do Sodré and Santos neighborhoods along the waterfront. Enjoy a sundowner at a riverside bar with views of the 25 de Abril Bridge (reminiscent of San Francisco's Golden Gate). Have dinner in the area.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Cais do Sodré station café before the train — coffee and pastel de nata ~€2.
meals.lunch: Belém area — the Pastéis de Belém café also serves light lunch dishes. Alternatively, grab a sandwich and eat by the riverfront. Budget ~€7–9.
meals.dinner: Cais do Sodré area — try a petiscos (Portuguese tapas) bar for a budget-friendly spread of small plates: pão com manteiga (bread & butter), azeitonas (olives), queijo (cheese), and a main. Budget ~€13–16 with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Belém is about 6km west of downtown. The train from Cais do Sodré is the cheapest and fastest option. Combine the Jerónimos Monastery and Torre de Belém tickets for a potential discount (~€12 combined). Arrive at Pastéis de Belém before the lunch rush to avoid long queues.

day_by_day.morning: Spend your final morning exploring the LX Factory (Rua Rodrigues de Faria 103) — a repurposed 19th-century industrial complex now home to independent shops, street art, cafés, and creative spaces. Free to enter and wander. On Sundays it hosts a market, but on Tuesday the creative studios and cafés are open. Great for a relaxed final morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back to Baixa for last-minute exploration and souvenir shopping. Visit the free Elevador de Santa Justa (take the stairs up for free instead of paying ~€5.30 for the elevator) for rooftop views over the Baixa grid. Walk up to Chiado and browse independent bookshops and local ceramics stores. Pick up affordable souvenirs: tinned fish (conservas), local wine, or ceramic tiles from neighborhood shops.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Chiado or Bairro Alto — treat yourself slightly more on the last night while staying within budget. Look for a restaurant serving grilled sea bass (robalo) or arroz de marisco (seafood rice). Finish with a ginjinha (cherry liqueur shot ~€1.50) at a traditional ginjinha bar in Rossio square — a quintessential Lisbon farewell ritual.

meals.breakfast: LX Factory café — specialty coffee and a pastry in a cool industrial setting ~€4–5.
meals.lunch: Mercado de Campo de Ourique (indoor food market, Rua Coelho da Rocha) — affordable fresh market food stalls with local dishes ~€8–10. Take the 28E tram or a 15-min walk from LX Factory.
meals.dinner: Chiado or Bairro Alto restaurant — budget €15–18 for a full sit-down farewell meal with wine. Look for the ementa turística for best value.

day_by_day.notes: Check your flight departure time and plan accordingly — if flying out on the 19th evening, adjust the afternoon to allow time to return to the hotel, collect luggage, and head to the airport (allow at least 2.5 hours before departure). The Metro Red Line from Baixa-Chiado to the airport takes about 35 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the Aerobus or Metro (Red Line to Green Line) to central Lisbon. Check in to Lisbon City Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the immediate neighborhood on foot — stroll through Baixa-Chiado, Lisbon's elegant downtown grid. Visit Praça do Comércio by the Tagus waterfront, walk up to Rua Augusta Arch, and soak in the city's atmosphere at a relaxed pace. Stop at a local pastelaria for your first pastel de nata.
day_by_day.evening: Alfama Fado & Dinner Experience — head to the historic Alfama district for an intimate Fado music dinner. Enjoy traditional Portuguese dishes (bacalhau, caldo verde) paired with Portugal's soulful national music in a cozy casa de fado. Book in advance as tables fill quickly.

meals.breakfast: Grab a light snack at the airport or on arrival — coffee and a pastel de nata at a café near the hotel (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near Baixa: A Cevicheria or a local tasca — try a prego sandwich or bifanas (€10–15)
meals.dinner: Included in the Alfama Fado & Dinner Experience — traditional Portuguese multi-course dinner with wine (€45–65 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives at 13:00 — allow 60–90 minutes for airport transit and check-in. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Wear comfortable walking shoes as Lisbon has many cobblestone streets and hills.

day_by_day.morning: São Jorge Castle & Mouraria Walking Tour — start the day with a visit to the 11th-century Moorish castle of São Jorge. Enjoy panoramic views over Lisbon's red-roofed skyline and the Tagus River. Then descend through the vibrant Mouraria neighborhood, Lisbon's oldest and most multicultural quarter, learning about its Moorish and Fado heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Alfama on your own — visit the Museu do Fado to deepen your understanding of the previous night's music experience, then wander the narrow alleyways (becos) and miradouros (viewpoints) like Miradouro da Graça for stunning city views. Visit the Feira da Ladra flea market if it's running (Tuesdays and Saturdays).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Mouraria or Alfama at a traditional tasca. Try a local restaurant serving petiscos (Portuguese tapas) — dishes like pataniscas de bacalhau, alheira, and grilled sardines with a glass of vinho verde.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — coffee, toast with butter and jam, or a croissant (€4–7)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in Mouraria — try Zé da Mouraria or a similar neighborhood spot for a prato do dia (dish of the day) with bread, drink, and dessert (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Petiscos dinner at a Alfama tasca — shared small plates and house wine (€20–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: São Jorge Castle opens at 09:00 — arrive early to beat crowds. Wear sturdy shoes for the castle's uneven terrain. The Mouraria walking tour can be self-guided using maps from the tourist office or booked as a guided experience for added historical context.

day_by_day.morning: Belém Historical District & Pastéis de Belém — take Tram 15E or a rideshare (20 minutes from center) to Belém. Visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, a breathtaking example of Manueline architecture built to celebrate Portugal's Age of Discovery. Explore the cloisters and the tombs of Vasco da Gama and Luís de Camões.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Belém — walk to the iconic Tower of Belém on the Tagus riverbank and the Monument to the Discoveries. Visit the MAAT (Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology) or the Museu de Marinha if history of exploration interests you. End with a visit to the original Pastéis de Belém bakery (open since 1837) for the world-famous custard tarts dusted with cinnamon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon and head to the Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour — explore this iconic curated food hall in Cais do Sodré, sampling dishes from some of Lisbon's best chefs and producers. Perfect for a relaxed, exploratory dinner with plenty of variety.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel, then a mid-morning pastel de nata at Pastéis de Belém (the original!) — iconic and unmissable (€1.50 per tart)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Belém — sandwich or salad at a riverside café, or snack on more pastéis (€10–15)
meals.dinner: Time Out Market — budget €20–35 per person for a varied selection of dishes and a glass of wine or craft beer

day_by_day.notes: Jerónimos Monastery is closed on Mondays — if this is an issue, swap Day 3 and Day 4. Check opening hours before going. Belém is about 6 km west of the city center; the tram ride is scenic but can be slow — allow extra time.

day_by_day.morning: Mercado de Campo de Ourique & Príncipe Real Gourmet Walk — begin at the charming Campo de Ourique market, a beloved local neighborhood market away from tourist crowds. Browse stalls of fresh produce, cheese, charcuterie, and regional specialties. Chat with vendors and pick up snacks for the walk ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Self-guided Príncipe Real Gourmet Walk — stroll through the elegant Príncipe Real neighborhood, known for its independent boutiques, gourmet food shops, and antique dealers. Visit A Cevicheria or Mercearia do Príncipe for local delicacies. Explore the Jardim do Príncipe Real and the nearby Bairro Alto. Stop at a wine shop for a tasting of Portuguese wines — Douro reds, Alentejo whites, and Moscatel.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara (one of Lisbon's best viewpoints, just above Bairro Alto) — enjoy the golden hour view over the city. Afterward, dinner in Bairro Alto or Chiado at a mid-range restaurant. Try traditional Portuguese grilled fish or a modern Portuguese bistro.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at a local café in Campo de Ourique neighborhood (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Grazing lunch at Campo de Ourique Market — assemble your own spread of cheese, ham, olives, bread, and local wine (€12–18)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Chiado or Bairro Alto — restaurants like Taberna da Rua das Flores or similar mid-range tascas (€25–35 per person with wine)

day_by_day.notes: Campo de Ourique Market is open Tuesday–Sunday. The Príncipe Real area is hilly but walkable — take Tram 28 or a rideshare from the hotel if tired. This day is intentionally more relaxed for a balanced pace.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Tile Museum (Museu Nacional do Azulejo) — one of Lisbon's most unique and rewarding museums, housed in a former convent. Discover the history of Portugal's iconic blue-and-white azulejo tiles from the 15th century to the present. The museum also contains a stunning Manueline church and a panoramic tile panel of pre-earthquake Lisbon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the LX Factory — a former industrial complex turned creative hub in Alcântara, open all week but especially vibrant. Browse independent shops, art studios, bookstores, and design spaces. Enjoy a coffee or craft beer in one of the courtyard cafés. Afterward, take a final walk along the Tagus riverfront (Ribeira das Naus) and soak in the last views of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in the Chiado or Baixa area — splurge slightly on a memorable final meal at a quality Portuguese restaurant. Consider dishes like arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice), grilled sea bass, or leitão (roast suckling pig). Toast with a glass of ginjinha (cherry liqueur) at a traditional ginjinha bar.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a café near the hotel — galão (milky coffee), toast, and fruit (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Lunch at LX Factory — try one of the casual restaurants or food stalls inside the complex (€14–20)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a quality mid-range restaurant in Chiado — budget €35–50 per person for a special final evening with wine and dessert

day_by_day.notes: National Tile Museum is closed on Mondays and Tuesdays — this itinerary places it on Wednesday. If departing on Day 6, pack bags the night before. Keep the evening flexible in case of an early next-day flight. A small shot of ginjinha at A Ginjinha bar near Rossio is a classic Lisbon farewell ritual (€1.50).

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private transfer arranged from Humberto Delgado Airport to Lisbon City Stay hotel. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your luxury accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely exploration of the immediate hotel neighbourhood on foot. Stroll through Chiado and Bairro Alto, browsing elegant boutiques and soaking in the Pombaline architecture. Visit the iconic Livraria Bertrand (world's oldest operating bookshop) and enjoy a coffee at the legendary Café A Brasileira — a Belle Époque institution beloved by Lisbon's literary elite.
day_by_day.evening: Alfama Fado & Dinner Experience — immerse yourself in Portugal's soulful Fado tradition with an intimate, candlelit dinner at a premium Fado house. Enjoy traditional petiscos, slow-cooked bacalhau, and aged Dão wines while world-class Fadistas perform. Book a private table for the most exclusive experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the plane or a light welcome spread at the hotel upon check-in — request the hotel's afternoon welcome amenity (charcuterie, local cheeses, and a glass of Vinho Verde).
meals.lunch: Upon arrival, enjoy a late lunch at Taberna da Rua das Flores — a celebrated Lisbon tavern serving elevated Portuguese petiscos such as presunto ibérico, ameijoas à Bulhão Pato, and house-made bread with premium olive oil.
meals.dinner: Full dinner included as part of the Alfama Fado & Dinner Experience at a top-tier Fado house such as Clube de Fado or Tasca do Chico — expect a multi-course traditional Portuguese menu with wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Flight TP lands at 13:00 — allow approximately 45–60 minutes for immigration, baggage claim, and private transfer. Pre-arrange fast-track airport assistance for a seamless arrival. Confirm Fado dinner reservation well in advance as top venues book out weeks ahead. Dress code for Fado houses is smart-casual to elegant.

day_by_day.morning: São Jorge Castle & Mouraria Walking Tour — begin the day with a guided exploration of the 11th-century Moorish Castelo de São Jorge, perched atop Lisbon's highest hill. Enjoy sweeping panoramic views over the terracotta rooftops, the Tagus River, and the 25 de Abril Bridge. Descend through the labyrinthine streets of Mouraria, Lisbon's oldest and most atmospheric neighbourhood, with a knowledgeable local guide sharing stories of Moorish heritage, the birth of Fado, and multicultural history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour — head to the iconic Time Out Market in Cais do Sodré for a curated culinary journey through Lisbon's finest food stalls. Sample dishes from Michelin-starred chefs alongside artisan producers: try Henrique Sá Pessoa's signature bites, fresh Algarve oysters, traditional pastéis de bacalhau, and craft ginjinha. Pair tastings with premium Portuguese wines and natural wines from the Alentejo region.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset cruise on the Tagus River aboard a luxury sailboat or classic wooden vessel. Watch the golden light bathe the city skyline, the Cristo Rei statue, and the Jerónimos Monastery from the water. Return to shore for a refined dinner in Chiado.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — opt for the full à la carte menu featuring fresh pastries, smoked salmon, local cheeses, seasonal fruit, and freshly squeezed orange juice. Alternatively, visit Padaria Portuguesa in Chiado for an authentic local bakery experience.
meals.lunch: Grazing lunch at Time Out Market as part of the food tour — curated multi-tasting format covering savoury bites, seafood, charcuterie, and desserts. Budget approximately €40–60 per person for a thorough tasting experience.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Alma (Chef Henrique Sá Pessoa, Michelin-starred) in Chiado — an exquisite tasting menu celebrating the finest Portuguese ingredients with contemporary technique. Wine pairing with rare Douro and Alentejo vintages highly recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Book the São Jorge Castle tour for early morning (9:00–10:00 opening) to avoid weekend crowds. The Time Out Market is busiest at midday on Saturdays — consider arriving at 13:30 for a more relaxed experience. Sunset cruise should be pre-booked through a premium operator such as Lisbon Sailing or Secret Spot; departure typically around 18:30–19:00 in May.

day_by_day.morning: Belém Historical District — private guided tour of the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, a breathtaking masterpiece of Manueline Gothic architecture built to celebrate Vasco da Gama's voyage to India. Explore the ornate cloisters, royal tombs, and the soaring nave at a leisurely, exclusive pace. Walk along the Tagus waterfront to the iconic Torre de Belém, the 16th-century fortified tower that has stood sentinel over Lisbon's maritime gateway for five centuries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pastéis de Belém pilgrimage — visit the legendary Pastéis de Belém bakery (operating since 1837) for the original pastel de nata, still made from a secret recipe. Then visit the MAAT (Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology) for a curated contemporary art experience in a stunning riverside setting. Alternatively, explore the Museu Nacional dos Coches (National Coach Museum), home to the world's finest collection of royal carriages.
day_by_day.evening: Mercado de Campo de Ourique & Príncipe Real Gourmet Walk — as the day cools, explore the elegant Príncipe Real neighbourhood, Lisbon's most refined quarter. Browse antique dealers, designer boutiques, and artisan food shops. End the evening with cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the city before a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel followed by a mid-morning coffee stop at Café Versailles — a grand Art Deco café near Belém beloved by locals since 1922.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Feitoria (Michelin-starred), located inside the Altis Belém Hotel overlooking the Tagus River — Chef João Rodrigues' celebrated tasting menu focuses on Portuguese terroir and seasonal produce with exceptional river views.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bairro do Avillez (Chef José Avillez) in Chiado — a sophisticated multi-concept restaurant space offering a refined Portuguese menu in an elegant setting. Try the tasting menu in the upstairs Beco by Avillez for an intimate experience.

day_by_day.notes: Belém is approximately 6 km west of central Lisbon — arrange a private car or taxi for the morning transfer. Jerónimos Monastery is closed on Mondays, so Sunday is ideal. Pre-book skip-the-line tickets for the monastery. The Pastéis de Belém bakery can have long queues on weekends — arrive before 11:00 or after 15:00 for shorter waits.

day_by_day.morning: Sintra Day Excursion — take a private chauffeured car 30 km west of Lisbon to the UNESCO World Heritage village of Sintra, nestled in the misty Serra de Sintra hills. Visit the fairy-tale Palácio Nacional da Pena, perched dramatically on a rocky crag with its vivid polychrome facades, and explore the mystical Quinta da Regaleira with its initiation wells and Masonic symbolism. A knowledgeable private guide will bring the Romantic-era history to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Sintra with a visit to the Moorish Castle ruins offering panoramic Atlantic views, or the serene Palace of Monserrate with its extraordinary Moorish-Gothic-Indian architecture. In the late afternoon, drive to the westernmost point of continental Europe — Cabo da Roca — for dramatic clifftop views over the Atlantic Ocean before returning to Lisbon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lisbon for a relaxed evening. Enjoy cocktails at Park Bar — Lisbon's celebrated rooftop bar atop a parking garage in Bairro Alto with sweeping city views — before a late, leisurely dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the hotel before departure for Sintra — ensure an early start (by 09:00) to make the most of the day.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Tascas de Sintra or the upscale restaurant at Palácio de Seteais (a neoclassical palace-hotel) — an elegant setting for traditional Portuguese cuisine including roasted lamb, wild mushroom rice, and local Serra da Estrela cheese.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Belcanto (Chef José Avillez, two Michelin stars) in Chiado — Lisbon's most celebrated fine dining destination. The avant-garde tasting menu reimagines classic Portuguese flavours with extraordinary creativity. This is the pinnacle of Lisbon dining; reserve months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Sintra is best explored with a private guide and driver — public transport is possible but limiting. Book Pena Palace tickets online in advance as they sell out, especially on weekdays in May. Wear comfortable walking shoes as Sintra involves significant uphill walking. The Belcanto reservation is critical — contact the restaurant immediately upon booking this trip as tables are extremely limited.

day_by_day.morning: Mercado de Campo de Ourique & Príncipe Real Gourmet Walk — dedicate your final morning to Lisbon's most refined food and neighbourhood experience. Begin at the charming Mercado de Campo de Ourique, a beloved local covered market with artisan vendors selling heritage cheeses, cured meats, fresh bread, and seasonal produce. Chat with vendors, sample rare regional products, and pick up premium food souvenirs such as aged Queijo de Azeitão, Flor de Sal, premium olive oils, and vintage Port.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely final afternoon in Príncipe Real — explore the weekly antiques and design market in the garden, visit the elegant Embaixada concept store (housed in a stunning Moorish-revival palace), and browse independent galleries. Enjoy a final Ginjinha (sour cherry liqueur) at a traditional taberna. Return to the hotel for a relaxed check-out and luggage consolidation. Optional: visit the Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga (National Museum of Ancient Art) for world-class Portuguese painting and decorative arts.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a celebrated Lisbon restaurant before any onward travel arrangements. Spend the final hours on a rooftop terrace watching the Lisbon sunset paint the city in warm amber tones — a perfect conclusion to a premium Portuguese experience.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savour it slowly and request a special farewell amenity from the concierge (many luxury hotels offer a complimentary final-morning upgrade or champagne breakfast).
meals.lunch: Lunch at O Velho Eurico in Alfama — a hidden gem serving exceptional traditional Portuguese food with stunning views over the Tagus. Try the arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice) or grilled dourada (sea bream) with house wine.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Cervejaria Ramiro — Lisbon's legendary seafood institution, beloved by locals and visitors alike since 1956. Order the classic progression: fresh oysters, tiger prawns, percebes (barnacles), and finish with a steak sandwich (prego) as tradition dictates. Pair with chilled Alvarinho Vinho Verde.

day_by_day.notes: Campo de Ourique market is liveliest on Tuesday mornings. If departing Lisbon on the evening of Day 5, arrange a private transfer to the airport and factor in at least 2.5 hours before flight departure. Ask the hotel concierge to arrange premium food gift packaging for any market purchases. Consider leaving a small window for last-minute souvenir shopping at the Conserveira de Lisboa (historic tinned fish shop) — a uniquely Portuguese luxury gift.
